mechanism_builds.causal_path: Subject-specific autonomic tone, vascular compliance, and electrode-skin impedance create distinct marginal distributions of non-conformity scores → pooling calibration and test segments across subjects violates exchangeability → conditional coverage guarantee degrades
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Cross-subject calibration yields lower empirical coverage than within-subject calibration; coverage gap increases with KS distance between subject non-conformity score distributions
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Multi-subject physiological monitoring with no subject-level covariates in predictor
Calibration set drawn from different subjects than test segments
Signal modalities: ECG, PPG, or BP with subject-specific morphology
measurable_outcomes: Empirical coverage difference: within-subject vs cross-subject calibration (percentage points)
KS distance between non-conformity score CDFs across subjects
Coverage gap vs. subject physiological distance (e.g., PWV difference) correlation coefficient
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Test by constructing calibration sets from single vs. multiple subjects; measure non-conformity score distribution shift using Wasserstein distance; quantify coverage degradation as function of subject heterogeneity.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Segment-dependent motion artifacts, electrode pops, and baseline wander alter residual distribution shape → non-conformity score distribution shifts between clean and artifact segments → identical distribution assumption violated → coverage drops in high-artifact segments when calibrated on clean data
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage decreases monotonically with increasing artifact amplitude/rate; negative slope of coverage vs. artifact level when calibration from low-artifact segments
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Artifact labels unavailable for stratification
Segments defined by external protocol (e.g., fixed windows) not artifact state
Signal types: wearable PPG, ambulatory ECG, EEG with motion corruption
measurable_outcomes: Spearman correlation between segment artifact RMS and empirical coverage
Wasserstein distance between non-conformity score distributions in clean vs. artifact segments
Coverage deficit in top artifact quartile vs. bottom quartile (percentage points)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Induce controlled artifacts via motion protocols; measure non-conformity score distribution shift using sliced Wasserstein distance; test if artifact-aware non-conformity measures (e.g., residual/SNR) stabilize coverage.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Abrupt autonomic shifts (sleep-stage, orthostasis) alter signal morphology faster than calibration window adapts → calibration windows spanning transitions mix pre- and post-transition non-conformity scores → exchangeability violated within window → coverage degrades near transitions
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage lowest for segments centered on transitions; coverage decreases as proportion of transition-spanning calibration windows increases; pre-transition and post-transition coverage differ significantly
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: State changes at timescales shorter than calibration window (e.g., < 5 min for sleep stages)
Non-conformity measure sensitive to state-dependent features (HRV, PPG morphology)
Continuous monitoring with unobserved state transitions
measurable_outcomes: Empirical coverage in 30-sec bins relative to annotated transition time
Coverage difference between pure pre-transition and pure post-transition segments
Coverage vs. calibration window length for fixed transition rate
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Use polysomnography-annotated sleep stages or tilt-table orthostatic transitions; vary calibration window length; measure non-conformity score bimodality index (Hartigan's dip test) in transition-spanning windows.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Serial dependence in residuals induces clustering of non-conformity scores → effective sample size n_eff = n * (1-rho)/(1+rho) < nominal n → finite-sample coverage guarantee weakens → coverage fluctuates with segment-specific autocorrelation strength
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage deviation magnitude increases as AR(1) coefficient increases; coverage variance across segments positively correlated with segment autocorrelation; nominal coverage achieved only when n_eff > threshold (e.g., 30)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Segment length insufficient for mixing (e.g., < 10x autocorrelation decay time)
Non-conformity scores not decorrelated (e.g., absolute residuals of ARMA process)
Physiological signals: ECG R-R intervals, PPG pulse rate, continuous BP
measurable_outcomes: Regression slope of |coverage - nominal| vs. segment AR(1) coefficient
Effective sample size n_eff at which coverage enters nominal 95% CI
Coverage coefficient of variation across segments vs. mean segment autocorrelation
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Simulate AR(1) non-conformity scores with known rho; compute n_eff via batch means; test block conformal or thinning to restore exchangeability; measure coverage stability vs. block size.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Segment-varying annotation errors (R-peak jitter, sleep-stage disagreement) create heteroscedastic label noise → non-conformity scores biased proportionally to error variance → score distribution shifts differently per segment → coverage destabilizes
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage deviates from nominal in segments with high annotation error variance; direction of deviation follows annotation bias sign; coverage variance across segments correlates with annotation error variance
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Label noise characteristics differ across segments due to signal quality or annotator fatigue
Noise heteroscedasticity unmodeled in conformal procedure
Ground truth: manual R-peak annotation, sleep staging, BP cuff synchronization
measurable_outcomes: Correlation between segment annotation error variance (from replicate annotations) and coverage deviation
Median non-conformity score shift vs. induced annotation bias in controlled experiment
Coverage in high-SNR vs. low-SNR segments (using SNR as proxy for annotation quality)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Inject synthetic annotation jitter with known variance; compare coverage using clean vs. noisy labels; measure non-conformity score distribution shift via KL divergence; test noise-robust non-conformity measures (e.g., quantile regression residuals).

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Unmeasured covariates (medication, hydration, circadian phase) shift signal distribution and optimal prediction interval width → single non-conformity measure applied across all segments → miscalibration where covariate composition differs from calibration set → coverage varies with latent covariate distribution
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage deviates in segments with different latent covariate distributions vs. calibration; coverage gap correlates with MMD between segment and calibration covariate distributions; stratified coverage reveals systematic under/over-coverage in specific covariate strata
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Latent covariates unrecorded but vary systematically across recording sessions/segments
Covariates modulate signal predictability (e.g., beta-blockers reduce HRV, dehydration increases BP variability)
No randomization possible in observational physiological monitoring
measurable_outcomes: Coverage difference between medication-on vs. medication-off segments (post-hoc stratification)
Maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between segment and calibration covariate distributions vs. coverage gap
Calibration of adaptive conformal prediction with estimated propensity scores for latent covariates
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Collect latent covariates in sub-study; use MMD to quantify covariate shift; test weighted conformal prediction with importance weights; measure coverage improvement when stratifying by observed proxies (time-of-day, medication logs).

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Variable artifact rejection/missing data causes effective calibration size n_cal to vary across segments → smaller n_cal yields wider prediction sets and higher coverage variance (finite-sample effect) → when n_cal correlates with segment characteristics (e.g., activity level), coverage appears unstable but reflects sample-size artifacts
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage variance inversely proportional to n_cal; mean coverage conservative (over-coverage) for small n_cal due to quantile inflation; apparent instability correlates with artifact rejection rate
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration size varies systematically with segment characteristics (e.g., more artifacts during exercise)
Adaptive windowing or artifact rejection creates heterogeneous n_cal
Nominal coverage target: 90% or 95%
measurable_outcomes: Empirical coverage variance across segments vs. theoretical finite-sample variance (1/(n_cal+1))
Regression of segment coverage on n_cal controlling for segment type
Coverage stability after subsampling all segments to equal n_cal
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Subsample calibration sets to fixed n_cal to isolate distribution shift from sample size effects; compare observed coverage variance to binomial variance; test if coverage instability persists after equalizing n_cal across segments.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Segments with complex morphologies (arrhythmia, motion-corrupted PPG) exhibit heavy-tailed, heteroscedastic residuals; clean segments have near-Gaussian errors → fixed non-conformity measure (absolute residual) cannot normalize shape variation → over-coverage in simple segments, under-coverage in complex segments
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage negatively correlated with morphological complexity (sample entropy) and residual kurtosis; under-coverage in high-complexity segments, over-coverage in low-complexity segments
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Conditional error distribution varies in shape (kurtosis, skewness) not just scale across segments
Non-conformity measure fixed (e.g., |y - y_hat|) without local scaling
Signal types: ECG with arrhythmia, PPG with motion, EEG with seizures
measurable_outcomes: Spearman correlation between segment sample entropy and empirical coverage
Coverage in high-kurtosis (top quartile) vs. low-kurtosis (bottom quartile) segments
Coverage improvement using adaptive non-conformity: |residual| / local_MAD vs. fixed
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Compute local scale estimates (MAD, quantile regression) per segment; test locally adaptive non-conformity measures; measure coverage uniformity across complexity strata using chi-squared goodness-of-fit.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Gradual shifts in mean signal level, variability, or feature relationships (circadian, disease progression, sensor degradation) alter non-conformity score distribution over hours-days → calibration distribution becomes stale → coverage decays proportionally to drift magnitude and time since calibration; drift rate differs by modality
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage decreases monotonically with calibration window age; decay slope steeper for faster-drifting modalities (e.g., PPG > ECG); coverage restored by recalibration
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Drift timescale longer than calibration window (hours) but shorter than recording (days)
Drift rates differ across signal modalities (PPG more susceptible to sensor degradation)
No adaptive recalibration in baseline conformal procedure
measurable_outcomes: Coverage vs. hours since calibration (linear decay slope with 95% CI)
Drift rate estimation via sliding-window KS test on non-conformity scores
Modality-specific drift rates: PPG vs. ECG vs. BP coverage decay comparison
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Track non-conformity score distribution over 24-72h recordings; fit exponential decay to coverage; test periodic recalibration (e.g., every 4h) vs. adaptive windowing; quantify drift via Wasserstein distance between consecutive calibration windows.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Physiological oscillators (RSA ~0.2-0.3 Hz, Mayer waves ~0.1 Hz, thermoregulation ~24h) periodically modulate prediction error variance → non-conformity score distribution varies with oscillator phase → segments captured at different phases have systematically different score distributions → coverage oscillates with segment timing relative to hidden phases
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage oscillates at confounder frequencies; lowest coverage at high-error-variance phases (e.g., inspiration for RSA, vasoconstriction for Mayer waves); circular correlation between segment boundary phase and coverage significant
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Multiple overlapping physiological rhythms modulate predictability
Segment boundaries determined by external protocol (fixed windows) not physiological phase
Non-conformity measure sensitive to phase-dependent error variance
measurable_outcomes: Circular correlation coefficient between segment start phase (from concurrent respiration/BP) and coverage
Spectral peak in coverage time series at Mayer wave frequency (0.1 Hz) or respiratory frequency
Coverage amplitude of oscillation (max-min coverage across phases)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Record concurrent respiration, continuous BP, temperature; compute instantaneous phase via Hilbert transform; bin segments by phase; test if phase-stratified conformal prediction stabilizes coverage; measure coverage oscillation amplitude via Rayleigh test.
